summary:
OrbitFit is a microgravity exercise companion developed to address one of the major challenges of long-duration space missions: muscle weakening and bone loss caused by reduced gravitational loading.

Our project is a web application that combines exercise management, health check-ins, and progress visualization to help astronauts monitor their physical condition throughout their missions.

Instead of treating exercise and health monitoring as separate activities, OrbitFit integrates them into one accessible platform. Astronauts can record their daily workouts, track sets, repetitions, resistance, and effort, and view their weekly training progress through interactive charts and a visual muscle map.

The platform also provides three levels of health monitoring. Daily check-ins record parameters such as heart rate, SpO2, fatigue, soreness, nutrition, and body mass. Weekly assessments track physical performance through grip strength, squat tests, and plank duration. Periodic scans can record muscle thickness and bone density when measurements are available.

By comparing these records over time, OrbitFit helps highlight declining strength, reduced muscle training, and changes in health indicators. It also suggests workouts for undertrained muscle groups.

OrbitFit is important because early awareness and consistent monitoring can support better exercise habits, informed health decisions, and astronaut well-being during extended space exploration.
details:
OrbitFit is a microgravity exercise companion that helps astronauts track their fitness and monitor potential muscle and bone loss during space missions.

The platform includes five sections for daily activity, workout logging, health checks, progress visualization, and data export. It tracks daily health indicators, weekly strength measurements, and periodic muscle and bone assessments. Interactive charts and a visual muscle map help astronauts understand their progress and identify areas needing attention.

OrbitFit benefits astronauts by bringing exercise management and health monitoring into one accessible platform. Its intended impact is to encourage consistent exercise and improve awareness of physical changes during long-duration missions.

It is developed as a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with manual data entry in the current prototype.

The innovative aspect is its integration of three-level health monitoring, visual muscle mapping, and suggested workouts. Our team considered the effects of microgravity, ease of use, exercise consistency, and the importance of tracking long-term health changes.
dataRefs: Effects of exercise countermeasures on multisystem function in long duration spaceflight astronauts
